question: Are lives still getting better now? Trend in the last decade versus the prior fifty years, by region.
class_rule: For each region: last10 is the slope of a straight line fitted to readings in [last_year-10, last_year]; prior50 is the same slope over [last_year-60, last_year-11]. Relative means slope divided by mean level in that window, carrying the slope's sign; each class applies the indicator's direction so that improving always means better. Improving if relative is above +0.2% per year; worsening if below -0.2% per year; stalled otherwise. Windows with 2 readings use the endpoint slope and are flagged sparse; fewer than 2 readings or a contested direction yield insufficient_data or unclassed.

metrics.label: Life expectancy at birth
metrics.source: UN World Population Prospects (2024), HMD (2025), Riley (2005), Zijdeman et al. (2015) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: US and UK series carry the 2015 to 2023 stall and the 2020 to 2021 reversal. ONS (Oct 22, 2024): England and Wales life expectancy in 2021 to 2023 was 26 weeks lower for males and 13 weeks lower for females than in 2017 to 2019, and 'since about 2011, the rate of increase in life expectancy has slowed'. CDC NCHS (Data Brief 521): US life expectancy 77.5 in 2022 and 78.4 in 2023, lower than UN WPP values here (78.0 and 79.3) because of different methods. World's last-ten-year slope is pulled down by the 2020 to 2021 pandemic dip; a second slope excluding those two years is stored alongside it.

metrics.label: Maternal mortality ratio
metrics.source: UN MMEIG (2023) via Our World in Data; CDC NCHS Health E-Stat (2023 rates)
metrics.notes: US regression: CDC NCHS rates rose from 17.4 (2018) to 32.9 (2021) before falling to 18.6 in 2023 (669 deaths). CDC series starts 2018 because NCHS changed coding (pregnancy checkbox); its last-10 class rests on six readings.

metrics.label: Under-five mortality rate
metrics.source: UN IGME (2025), Gapminder (2015) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: Converted from the source's unit, deaths per 100 live births, by multiplying by 10.

metrics.label: Adult obesity prevalence (BMI 30 or more, crude)
metrics.source: WHO Global Health Observatory (2026) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: Crude estimates, meaning not adjusted for age structure; WHO modelled series.

metrics.label: Drug overdose death rate, age-adjusted (US)
metrics.source: CDC NCHS Data Briefs 522, 457, 428, 394, 356, 329, 294 (National Vital Statistics System)
metrics.notes: Annual values assembled from successive NCHS data briefs; 2014 and 2004 to 2012 are not stated in those briefs. CDC provisional data (Feb 25, 2025): about 87,000 deaths in the 12 months to September 2024, down from around 114,000, nearly 24% lower, so the 2024 reading will fall well below 2023. No OECD-wide overdose series was found.

metrics.label: Suicide rate, age-standardized
metrics.source: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator MH_12 (Global Health Estimates)
metrics.notes: WHO regions plus United States, United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea. Global and most regional rates fall. WHO GHE shows the US rate rising to 14.3 in 2018 then dropping to 12.3 in 2020 and 2021; CDC NCHS (Data Brief 509, Sept 2024) instead reports 13.5 in 2020, 14.1 in 2021 and 14.2 in 2022, and reads: after increasing between 2002 to 2018, the age-adjusted suicide rate declined from 2018 through 2020 and then increased to 14.2 in 2022. The WHO-based US class (improving) is therefore doubtful; the CDC series is stored separately.

metrics.label: Adults who currently have or are being treated for depression (US)
metrics.source: Gallup National Health and Well-Being Index (May 17, 2023)
metrics.notes: Sparse: only the 2017 and 2023 readings are stated in Gallup's article. Gallup says 2023 is 'nearly 10 percentage points higher than in 2015' for lifetime diagnosis and 'up about seven points' for current depression. IHME depression prevalence series are not redistributable, so no world series.

metrics.label: Share of adults reporting loneliness
metrics.source: Gallup (Oct 14, 2024); Meta-Gallup State of Social Connections (Oct 24, 2023)

last_reading.region: World (very or fairly lonely, Meta-Gallup, 142 countries)

metrics.notes: US annual values are means of quarterly or monthly readings listed by Gallup (2021 includes its pandemic high of 25% in March). The world value is one reading from surveys run June 2022 to February 2023. No annual world series exists.

metrics.label: Average daily time spent using the internet
metrics.source: GWI via DataReportal Digital 2024 and Digital 2025 Global Overview

last_reading.region: World (internet users aged 16 to 64, GWI via DataReportal)

metrics.notes: World series covers internet users aged 16 to 64 (GWI via DataReportal), not all adults. Direction contested (more time online is not clearly better or worse), so no class. DataReportal: 6h40m at the start of 2024, 6h38m at the start of 2025, 6h36m in 2023 and 6h38m in late 2019; 2017 and 2018 were 'meaningfully higher' but not quantified. Shown in this atlas in place of its screen-time shadow card, which carries identical DataReportal readings; the merged row keeps its contested direction.

metrics.label: Median income or consumption per day (PPP 2021 dollars); US inflation-adjusted median household income
metrics.unit: international dollars per day (US series: 2024 dollars per year)
metrics.source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026) via Our World in Data; US Census Bureau via FRED (MEHOINUSA672N)
metrics.notes: US household series uses a different unit (annual inflation-adjusted household income) and is kept separate; its class is computed on its own scale. World Bank PIP projections beyond 2025 were dropped.

metrics.label: Gini coefficient of income or consumption
metrics.source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: Country-level only; World Bank publishes no world Gini, which measures inequality from 0 to 1, where 0 means everyone has equal income. Consolidated income or consumption series; breaks in survey comparability are possible.

metrics.label: Labor productivity: output per hour worked
metrics.unit: international dollars (2021 prices) per hour; US series index 2017=100
metrics.source: Penn World Table 11 via Our World in Data; US BLS via FRED (OPHNFB)
metrics.notes: Growth, not level, is what this question asks; compare relative slopes per year over the last ten years and the prior fifty.

metrics.label: PISA mean mathematics score
metrics.source: OECD PISA (2023) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: Triennial test (2003 to 2022, with 2022 delayed by the pandemic). OECD average fell from 489 (2018) to 472 (2022). Last-10 window holds 2012, 2015, 2018 and 2022.

metrics.label: Median house price to median household income
metrics.source: US: Census/HUD median sales price (MSPUS, annual mean of quarters) divided by Census median household income (MEHOINUSA646N), both via FRED; England: ONS housing affordability 2024

last_reading.region: United States (median new-home sale price / median household income)

metrics.notes: US ratio computed here from two FRED series. ONS (Mar 24, 2025): England 7.7 and Wales 5.9 in 2024; the ratio 'doubled from 1997 to 2007' (values not stated in that bulletin). No OECD-wide price-to-income series was found.

metrics.label: Deaths attributable to ambient air pollution, age-standardized rate (all causes)
metrics.source: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator AIR_42 (2021); Health Effects Institute State of Global Air 2024
metrics.notes: Ambient (outdoor) pollution only. WHO publishes only its 2021 estimate in this indicator, so no trend can be computed from redistributable data (IHME series are not redistributable). WHO global 2021 count (AIR_41): about 4.2 million ambient deaths. HEI (ambient plus household): 'Air pollution accounted for 8.1 million deaths globally in 2021', including more than 700,000 children under five.

metrics.label: Share of population living below $3.00 a day (2021 PPP)
metrics.source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: World Bank international poverty line of $3.00 a day in 2021 prices (updated June 2025). World values after 2022 are World Bank nowcasts, meaning estimates for years whose survey data are not yet in; projections beyond 2025 were dropped.

metrics.label: Share of population with access to electricity
metrics.source: World Bank (SDG 7 tracking) via Our World in Data

metrics.label: Population using safely managed drinking-water services
metrics.source: WHO/UNICEF JMP via WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator WSH_WATER_SAFELY_MANAGED
metrics.notes: WHO regions and global, total residence.

metrics.label: One-year-olds with three doses of DTP vaccine
metrics.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC (2026) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: World coverage plateaued in the mid 80s percent from about 2010, dipped in 2020 to 2021 and recovered partially.

metrics.label: Deaths attributable to bacterial antimicrobial resistance
metrics.source: GBD 2021 Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, The Lancet (Sept 2024)
metrics.notes: Sparse: only the 1990 and 2021 estimates are stated in the paper's findings, which say 2021 was 'a decrease in both estimates from 2019'. Attributable deaths are those resistance caused; associated deaths are those where resistance was present. Forecast: 1.91 million attributable and 8.22 million associated deaths in 2050. Under-five AMR deaths fell more than 50% over 1990 to 2021; deaths at 70 and older rose more than 80%. Classed insufficient_data by this atlas's rule (one reading in its last-ten-year window); 1990 to 2021 endpoints read worsening for attributable and stalled for associated deaths.

metrics.label: Road traffic death rate
metrics.source: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator RS_198 (Global Health Estimates)
metrics.notes: WHO regions and global plus United States, United Kingdom, India and China. WHO GHE's United States value (18.4 in 2023) sits well above NHTSA's fatality rate per 100,000 population; it is kept as published.

metrics.label: CO2 emissions per capita (fossil and industry)
metrics.source: Global Carbon Budget (2025) via Our World in Data
metrics.notes: Territorial emissions; excludes land-use change.

metrics.label: Share of population using the internet
metrics.source: ITU via World Bank via Our World in Data
